newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee firm, ends near high on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee firm, ends near high on fresh buying.

text.p: LIFFE coffee futures firmed to end near highs helped by buying interest from the trade, along with roasters and speculators, traders said.
Most active March last traded at $1,346, $15 higher, having seen a high of $1,350.
March volume was 3,805 of a total of 7,705 lots.
The exception to the rises was for January 1998, which last traded $5 lower at $1,285. However, just two lots of January 1998 traded all day.

Assisting London's gains was the firmness of the New York market, but buyers' assumption that now was the time to build up positions ahead of future rises was the main cause of the rise, one trader said. "People are watching strong arabica futures and wondering whether the same thing couldn't happen here," he said.
The view was, to some extent, contradicted by technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research of Cambridge in her latest weekly report.
"It is tempting to imagine current price activity as a potential base. However, it seems premature to look for sustainable gains to emerge yet," Gifford said.
The buyers were not finding their interest matched by any major origin selling, the trader said.
The news that the Colombian dock workers strike remains unsettled helped New York futures to firm in early trading. But origin selling into the rise trimmed gains.
The Colombian dock strike has paralysed about 160,000, 60 kg bags' worth of coffee exports, a top coffee official said on Friday.

Colombian Labour ministry officials were due to arrive in the Pacific coast port of Buenaventura on Friday in a bid to negotiate an end to the three-day old dock workers' strike that has shutdown much of Colombia's export sector, local media reports said.
A preliminary accord aimed at ending the strike was reached early on Thursday, but workers rejected it at a meeting later in the day.
